# Review — Development Project Manager

**Reviewer role:** Development Project Manager (PM-style delivery review)
**Date:** 2026-10-27
**Feature folder:** `docs/spec-001-feature/`
**Inputs reviewed (read in full):** `contract.md`, `brief.md`, `docs/spec-001-feature/feature-specification.md`, `docs/spec-001-feature/implementation-plan.md`, `docs/spec-001-feature/draft.md`, `docs/spec-001-feature/tasks/T1-core-analysis.md`, `docs/spec-001-feature/tasks/T2-cli-entry-point.md`, `docs/spec-001-feature/tasks/T3-contract-test-matrix.md`, `docs/spec-001-feature/README.md`, `docs/spec-001-feature/handoff.md`
**Environment verified:** Python 3.13.15, pytest 9.0.3 present at repo root (validation commands are runnable as written).
**Scope of this review:** identify gaps only. No plan/task/spec file was modified.

## Findings

| ID | Dimension | Severity | Finding | Suggested fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Coverage | Warning | AC3 requires "each row of 5.8" to be verified, but the **exit-1 internal-error row** (`Unexpected internal error \| 1 \| internal error`, D6/A1) has no test in any task. T2 implements the catch-all (`wordstat: error: internal error`, exit 1) and asserts no-Traceback for exit 2/3 cases only; T3's matrix lists only exit-2/exit-3 fixtures. | Add one test (T2 or T3) that triggers the catch-all (e.g. monkeypatch `analyze` in-process and call `main()`) asserting exit 1, empty stdout, exact single stderr line `wordstat: error: internal error\n`, no `Traceback`; or narrow AC3 wording to the end-to-end rows and state explicitly where the exit-1 path is proven. |
| F2 | Coverage | Warning | `draft.md` coverage matrix is internally inconsistent on **AC1**: the forward row lists "T2, T3" but the reverse check lists `T1 ← ... AC1`. T1 does pin the goldens at formatter level (T1 AC: `format_text`/`format_json` byte-equal to the contract examples). | Make forward and reverse agree: add T1 to the AC1 row (exit-0 evidence stays T2), or drop AC1 from T1's reverse list. |
| F3 | Coverage | Warning | Matrix attribution omits T2 where the behavior actually lives: **AC7** row says "T1, T3" and **AC10** row says "T1, T3", but the BOM-strip and no-newline-normalization behavior is T2's read path — contradicting draft.md's own decisions table (D1 "Implemented in: T2 (read path)"; D4 "T2 (decode)"). **R4** row says "T1" only although `--top` default 3 is implemented and tested in T2 (AC5). | Update the AC7/AC10 rows (and R4) to include T2 for delivery, keeping T3 as the end-to-end verifier; keep the reverse check in sync. |
| F4 | Coverage | Warning | `feature-specification.md` §5.3 normative token-table literals do not match their labels (verified at code-point level): row `"K"` (U+212A KELVIN SIGN) contains plain ASCII `K` (U+004B); row `"hello…world"` (mid-file U+FEFF) contains U+200D ZWJ, not U+FEFF. Expected tokens coincide by accident, so a literal copy-paste silently tests the wrong characters and would miss AC8's Kelvin case and AC7's mid-file-BOM case in unit tests. T1's notes name the code points correctly ("U+212A → `k`", "mid-file U+FEFF"), which partially compensates. | Replace the two table literals with the six-character ASCII escapes spelled backslash-u212A and backslash-uFEFF, and have T1/T3 require those escapes rather than copy-paste from the table. (T3's BOM fixture already uses `b"\xef\xbb\xbf"` — keep it.) |
| F5 | Coverage | Suggestion | G2 claims byte-for-byte determinism "on Windows, macOS and Linux", but all validation runs on the host OS only (here Windows). The design defends it (byte asserts, explicit total sort, `reconfigure`), but no task can prove other platforms. | Record in the plan/DoD that cross-platform determinism is by-design and host-verified only; optionally add a CI matrix later. No task change required. |
| F6 | Sequencing | Suggestion | T2's gate is `python -m pytest tests/test_cli.py -q` only, so a T2 change that breaks T1 core behavior is not caught until T3. (T2 is told core is out of scope, so risk is low.) | Make T2's validation `python -m pytest tests/test_core.py tests/test_cli.py -q` (or the full suite) so each gate covers everything built so far. |
| F7 | Scope | Warning | No task or plan step establishes the **pytest prerequisite**. All three validation commands assume pytest is installed; on a fresh environment T1's gate fails with no guidance. (Current repo env is fine: Python 3.13.15 + pytest 9.0.3, verified.) | Add a one-line prep item (plan §6 or T1 preamble): verify `python -c "import pytest"` (install via `pip install pytest` if missing) before T1 validation. |
| F8 | Scope | Suggestion | D2 (stderr reconfigured to UTF-8/`\n` so non-ASCII paths are byte-stable) has no fixture proving it: draft.md claims "Verified by: T3 (stderr byte asserts)", but T2/T3 fixture lists use ASCII paths only. | Add one `tmp_path` fixture with a non-ASCII filename (e.g. missing `tëst.txt` → exit 3) asserting exact stderr bytes. |
| F9 | Scope | Suggestion | AC11's "package imports nothing outside the standard library (pytest only in tests)" appears in T3's AC with no stated verification mechanism — it could pass as a manual claim. | Specify the check in T3 (e.g. a test importing `wordstat`/`wordstat.__main__` and asserting no third-party modules in `sys.modules`, or an import grep in T3's validation). |
| F10 | Scope | Suggestion | Package status is stale: `README.md` and `handoff.md` still say "Next: /geeky-plan" / "Spec written — not yet planned" (same stale status on `feature-specification.md` line 3) although plan and tasks now exist; `handoff.md` names `references.md` in the frozen set but no such file exists. | Refresh statuses to "planned — ready for plan-review"; either add `references.md` or drop it from the frozen list in `handoff.md`. |

## Per-dimension verdicts

### Coverage — Pass with notes

Verified: every R1–R6, G1–G4 and AC1–AC11 in `feature-specification.md` maps to at least one task body (not only the matrix row): R1→T2 AC4; R2→T2 read/stdin rules + T3 stdin guard; R3/R4→T1 formulas and `(-count, word)` sort; R5→T1 formatters + T2 `--json` wiring; R6→T2 dual `reconfigure` + T3 PYTHONHASHSEED matrix; G1–G4 all multi-task. Every `contract.md` clause is addressed somewhere: prog name, `--top >= 1`, both exact formats (incl. bare `top:`, JSON key order, trailing `\n`), the full exit-code table, `utf-8-sig`, stdin-never-read, empty-file exit 0, and the contract example goldens (sample with trailing newline, `chars: 33` arithmetic checked). Spot-checks of matrix claims against task bodies are mostly truthful (AC2/AC5/AC6/AC9/AC10 wording matches task ACs), with the exceptions F2–F4, and one true coverage gap (F1, exit-1 row). G2's cross-platform claim is host-verified only (F5).

### Sequencing — Pass with notes

Verified: T1→T2→T3 is the correct build order (pure core first, CLI glue second, evidence matrix last); each task's tests validate its own deliverable before the next starts (T1 in-process units need nothing; T2 subprocess tests need T1's `analyze`/`format_*`; T3 consumes both). All three validation commands are runnable from the repo root as written on Python 3.11+ with pytest (`python -m pytest tests/test_core.py -q`, `python -m pytest tests/test_cli.py -q`, `python -m pytest -q`), plus harmless `python -m compileall wordstat -q` and the `--help` smoke. One hardening note: F6 (T2 gate should also re-run core tests).

### Dependencies — Pass

Verified complete and consistent: T1 `Dependencies: None`; T2 `Dependencies: T1-core-analysis`; T3 `Dependencies: T1-core-analysis, T2-cli-entry-point` — matching plan §5 (including "T3 also consumes T1 for in-process fixtures") and the draft reverse check. Dependency names match the task file basenames. No circular or missing dependencies. The only cross-document inconsistency is coverage attribution (F2/F3), not the dependency fields.

### Scope — Pass with notes

Verified: all five deliverable paths are exactly the files the tasks will create — `wordstat/__init__.py` (T1), `wordstat/__main__.py` (T2), `tests/test_core.py` (T1), `tests/test_cli.py` (T2), `tests/test_contract.py` (T3) — matching plan §3 and the contract's flat `wordstat/` layout (no `src/`). Edge cases named by the contract are covered (empty/BOM-only, CRLF `chars: 36`, mid-file U+FEFF, four invalid-UTF-8 sequences, splitlines boundaries, U+0130 pre-lower `chars`, tie order, extra args / `-` literal / bad `--top`). No material over-scoping: T3's `.gitignore` `.pytest_cache/` line and T1's `compileall` are harmless housekeeping; D2's stderr `reconfigure` is a deliberate superset of contract R6 (which mandates stdout only) aligned with the brief's determinism demand, recorded as a decision — not silent scope creep. Real scope gaps: F7 (pytest prep), F8 (non-ASCII path fixture), F9 (stdlib-only check mechanism); hygiene: F10.

## Sanity checks

- **Paths:** confirmed — see Scope verdict; all five created files named consistently in plan §3, task scopes and draft architecture.
- **Estimates:** T1=M, T2=M, T3=M is realistic (small product code, heavy pinning/evidence work; T3 is the largest test-writing task). No re-estimation needed.
- **Decisions D1–D9:** applied consistently across spec/plan/tasks/handoff — D1 (CRLF `chars: 36`, bytes decode) in T1 notes, T2 read path, T3 fixture; D2 both streams in T2; D3 custom `--top` type in T2; D4 leading-BOM-only in T1/T2/T3; D5 last-line `^wordstat: error: ` assert in T2; D6 exit-1 wording in T2 (untested, F1); D7 precedence (`--top 0 missing.txt` → 2) in T2; D8 one FILE / `-` literal in T2; D9 zeroed empty output in T1/T3 goldens. No decision is contradicted anywhere; the only misalignments are matrix attribution (F2/F3) and two wrong spec-table literals (F4).

## Overall verdict

**APPROVED WITH NOTES**

No Critical findings. The package is implementable in order and covers `contract.md` substantively. Before or during implementation the orchestrator should resolve F1, F2, F3, F4 (coverage/matrix accuracy) and F7 (pytest prep); F5, F6, F8, F9, F10 are recommended hardening/hygiene.

2. **draft.md matrix not fully truthful (F2, F3)** — fix: align AC1 forward/reverse; add T2 to AC7/AC10/R4 rows to match the decisions table; keep reverse check in sync.
3. **Wrong literals in spec §5.3 token table (F4)** — fix: write the rows with the escapes spelled backslash-u212A and backslash-uFEFF in place of the plain ASCII letter K and U+200D; require those escapes in T1/T3 fixtures.
4. **pytest prerequisite not pinned (F7)** — fix: prep check/install note before T1 validation (env currently satisfied: Python 3.13.15, pytest 9.0.3).
5. **No non-ASCII path fixture to prove D2 (F8)** — fix: one non-ASCII filename error-path fixture with exact stderr bytes.
6. **AC11 stdlib-only claim has no verification mechanism (F9)** — fix: specify the import check in T3.
7. **G2 cross-platform claim host-verified only (F5)** — fix: record the limitation in DoD; optional CI matrix.

9. **Stale package status / phantom `references.md` (F10)** — fix: refresh README/handoff/spec status lines; add or drop `references.md`.

Task Name:
T2 — CLI entry point (argparse, streams, errors, exit codes) with subprocess tests

Context:
With the pure core locked (T1), `wordstat/__main__.py` must expose the exact
command-line contract: `python -m wordstat [--json] [--top N] FILE` from the repo
root, R1/R2/R5/R6 wiring, and the exit-code/error table of `contract.md` — clean
messages on stderr, empty stdout on error, never a traceback. This is the task
that makes the tool invocable and shapes every byte the user sees (AC1, AC3–AC6,
AC9).

Scope:

In scope:
---
- `wordstat/__main__.py`: `main(argv=None) -> int` plus
  `if __name__ == "__main__": raise SystemExit(main())`:
  - Startup: `sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")` and the same
    for `sys.stderr` (R6 + Decision D2), before any read/write.
  - `argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="wordstat")` with `--json` (store_true),
    `--top` (custom `type=` accepting int-strings >= 1, raising
    `argparse.ArgumentTypeError` otherwise; default 3), one required FILE.
  - Read the file as bytes and `decode("utf-8-sig")` (strict, no newline
    translation — Decision D1); never read stdin; `<path>` echoed exactly as given.
  - Error mapping per `contract.md` §Exit codes: OSError → exit 3
    `wordstat: error: <path>: cannot read file`; UnicodeDecodeError → exit 3
    `wordstat: error: <path>: not valid UTF-8`; argparse usage errors keep stock
    behavior (exit 2, last stderr line matches `^wordstat: error: ` — D5);
    catch-all `Exception` → `wordstat: error: internal error`, exit 1 (D6).
  - Success: print `format_text` or `format_json` result to stdout, exit 0.
- `tests/test_cli.py`: subprocess tests via
  `subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "wordstat", *args], capture_output=True,
  input=..., cwd=REPO_ROOT, timeout=30)` comparing raw bytes.

## Out of scope:
- Core counting/format logic (T1 owns it; CLI calls `analyze`/`format_*`).
- PYTHONHASHSEED determinism matrix, CRLF/BOM edge fixture suite, stdin-guard
  matrix beyond one smoke case (T3).
- Packaging, console scripts, configuration files.

Module/System:
`wordstat` package CLI layer (`__main__.py`); CLI tests in `tests/test_cli.py`.

## Dependencies:

* T1-core-analysis

## Technical Notes:
- `prog="wordstat"` is load-bearing (§5.6): without it, argparse uses
  `__main__.py` (≤3.13) or `python -m wordstat` (3.14+) and the contract's
  `^wordstat: error: ` prefix breaks. Assert `usage: wordstat` in `--help`.
- `--top` validator (Decision D3): `type=int` alone accepts `--top 0` (verified);
  use a custom callable raising `argparse.ArgumentTypeError`. Rejected values:
  `0`, `-1`, `abc`, `1.5`, missing value → each exit 2. `--top 1` and `--top=5`
  work. Error line shape: `wordstat: error: argument --top: <message>`.
- Usage errors print argparse's usage line(s) THEN the error line; tests assert
  the **last** stderr line against `^wordstat: error: ` (D5), not single-line.
  Exit-3 errors are exactly one stderr line ending in `\n`.
- Error precedence (D7): argparse runs first — `--top 0 missing.txt` exits 2,
  not 3. A missing file with valid args exits 3.
- stdout must be byte-empty (`b""`) on every error path; assert
  `b"Traceback" not in result.stderr` for every error case.
- `-` as FILE is a literal filename (R2: stdin never read) — missing `-` is
  exit 3 `cannot read file`. Extra positionals → exit 2 (unrecognized arguments).
- Reconfigure must happen before I/O (`io.UnsupportedOperation` if the stream was
  already read). Under subprocess tests the streams are real pipes, so reconfigure
  is what makes `\n` bytes deterministic on Windows.
- Derive `REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]` in tests; pass
  `cwd=REPO_ROOT`; never set `PYTHONSAFEPATH` (it would break `-m` resolution).
- Wire `--json` to `format_json`, default to `format_text` (R5); both come from T1.

## Acceptance Criteria:

* `python -m wordstat --help` exits 0 with help on stdout containing
  `usage: wordstat` and empty stderr (AC4).
* Contract example passes through the CLI byte-exactly:
  text golden `lines: 3\nwords: 8\nchars: 33\ntop: cat=2 the=2 a=1\n`;
  `--json --top 2` golden
  `{"lines": 3, "words": 8, "chars": 33, "top": [{"word": "cat", "count": 2}, {"word": "the", "count": 2}]}\n` (AC1).
* Error matrix (AC3): missing file / directory / unreadable → exit 3, stderr
  `wordstat: error: <path>: cannot read file\n`; invalid UTF-8 → exit 3,
  `wordstat: error: <path>: not valid UTF-8\n`; usage errors (no FILE, unknown
  flag, extra arg, bad `--top`) → exit 2 with last stderr line matching
  `^wordstat: error: `; stdout `b""` and no `Traceback` in all error cases.
* `--top` values `0`, `-1`, `abc`, `1.5`, and a missing value each exit 2;
  default `--top` is 3 (AC5).
* Empty file succeeds with zeroed output through the CLI (AC2 smoke).
* stdin is never read: with FILE + piped stdin the output is unchanged; without
  FILE the process exits 2 (no hang) (AC9).
* All tests in `tests/test_cli.py` pass.

Definition of Done:

* Code reviewed (phase review / impl-review evidence recorded)
* Tested (subprocess: `tests/test_cli.py`)
* Validation evidence recorded in `tasks/T2-cli-entry-point.notes.md` with
  commands, outputs and revision

- `python -m wordstat --help` exits 0 (smoke, from the repository root)

Task Name:
T1 — Core analysis module (counting, top words, formatters) with unit tests

Context:
`wordstat` must produce exact counts (R3), exact top-word ordering (R4) and exact
output strings (R5) from decoded text. The pure core is built and pinned by unit
tests before any CLI wiring exists, so the contract's counting/token semantics are
locked down independently of argparse, streams and exit codes. Supports the
contract example and every acceptance criterion about counts and formats
(AC1, AC2, AC7, AC8, AC10) as far as in-process evidence can.

Scope:

In scope:
---
- `wordstat/__init__.py`: pure functions only —
  - `analyze(text: str, top_n: int) -> dict` returning keys in order `lines`,
    `words`, `chars`, `top`, where `top` is a list of `{"word": str, "count": int}`
    (inner keys in that order).
  - `format_text(result: dict) -> str` — exactly four `\n`-terminated lines
    (`lines: `, `words: `, `chars: `, `top: `); empty top line is exactly `top:`
    with no trailing space.
  - `format_json(result: dict) -> str` — `json.dumps(result)` with default
    separators + trailing `\n`.
- `tests/test_core.py`: in-process pytest unit tests for the formulas, the token
  table, splitlines examples, top ordering and both formatters' exact output.

## Out of scope:
- `wordstat/__main__.py`, argparse, exit codes, stream reconfiguration (T2).
- Subprocess/CLI contract tests, determinism matrix, BOM/CRLF fixture files (T3).
- Any deviation from `contract.md` counting semantics (e.g. no `str.isalpha`,
  no `\w` word rule, no Unicode segmentation).

Module/System:
`wordstat/` package pure core (importable without side effects); tests in `tests/`.

## Dependencies:

* None

## Technical Notes:
- Formulas are normative (`feature-specification.md` §5.3): `lines =
  len(text.splitlines())`; `words = len(re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", text.lower()))`;
  `chars = len(text)` on the **original** decoded text — computed BEFORE lowering
  (`len('İ'.lower()) == 2`, so lowering first would corrupt `chars`).
- Token table to pin (§5.3): `"don't"` → `don`,`t`; `"ab-cd"` → `ab`,`cd`;
  `"42"` → `42`; `"café"` → `caf`; `"İstanbul"` → `i`,`stanbul`; U+212A → `k`;
  mid-file U+FEFF splits tokens but counts as 1 char (Decision D4).
- `chars` counts code points of the decoded text with no newline normalization
  (Decision D1) — a CRLF string's `\r` counts; `analyze` receives the decoded
  string as-is and must not translate anything.
- Top ordering: sort by `(-count, word)`, take first `top_n`; `top_n` comes from
  `--top` (default 3) and is assumed >= 1 (validated at CLI, T2). Fewer distinct
  words than `top_n` lists all (no error).
- `format_json` must use `json.dumps` **default** separators (`", "`, `": "`),
  no `sort_keys`/`indent`/`separators` overrides; dict insertion order provides
  the contract key order. Output of both formatters is pure ASCII for `[a-z0-9]+`
  tokens, but return `str` and let the CLI encode (streams are reconfigured in T2).
- Golden (contract example, trailing newline included): `analyze("The cat sat.\nThe cat ran!\nA dog.\n", 3)` →
  `lines=3, words=8, chars=33`, `top=[cat=2, the=2, a=1]`;
  `format_text` → `lines: 3\nwords: 8\nchars: 33\ntop: cat=2 the=2 a=1\n`;
  `format_json` (top 2) → `{"lines": 3, "words": 8, "chars": 33, "top": [{"word": "cat", "count": 2}, {"word": "the", "count": 2}]}\n`.
- Empty text: `analyze("", n)` → `0, 0, 0`, `top=[]`; `format_text` ends with
  `top:\n`; `format_json` has `"top": []` (Decision D9).
- Keep `__init__.py` free of CLI/IO imports; stdlib only (`re`, `collections`,
  `json`).

## Acceptance Criteria:

* `analyze` returns the exact dict shape and key order; counts match the R3
  formulas for the golden example and every §5.3 example (incl. `İstanbul` →
  2 words, CRLF `chars` = 4 for `"a\r\nb"`, `'a\n'` → 1 line, `'a\n\n'` → 2).
* Top list is ordered count-desc then word-asc with ties resolved alphabetically;
  `top_n` larger than distinct count returns all; JSON-shape entries are
  `{"word", "count"}` in that key order.
* `format_text` produces exactly the four contract lines ending in `\n`, and bare
  `top:` (no trailing space) when there are no words.
* `format_json` matches `json.dumps(...)` default separators + `\n`, byte-equal

* All unit tests in `tests/test_core.py` pass.

Task Name:
T2 — CLI entry point (argparse, streams, errors, exit codes) with subprocess tests

Context:
With the pure core locked (T1), `wordstat/__main__.py` must expose the exact
command-line contract: `python -m wordstat [--json] [--top N] FILE` from the repo
root, R1/R2/R5/R6 wiring, and the exit-code/error table of `contract.md` — clean
messages on stderr, empty stdout on error, never a traceback. This is the task
that makes the tool invocable and shapes every byte the user sees (AC1, AC3–AC6,
AC9).

Scope:

In scope:
---
- `wordstat/__main__.py`: `main(argv=None) -> int` plus
  `if __name__ == "__main__": raise SystemExit(main())`:
  - Startup: `sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")` and the same
    for `sys.stderr` (R6 + Decision D2), before any read/write.
  - `argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="wordstat")` with `--json` (store_true),
    `--top` (custom `type=` accepting int-strings >= 1, raising
    `argparse.ArgumentTypeError` otherwise; default 3), one required FILE.
  - Read the file as bytes and `decode("utf-8-sig")` (strict, no newline
    translation — Decision D1); never read stdin; `<path>` echoed exactly as given.
  - Error mapping per `contract.md` §Exit codes: OSError → exit 3
    `wordstat: error: <path>: cannot read file`; UnicodeDecodeError → exit 3
    `wordstat: error: <path>: not valid UTF-8`; argparse usage errors keep stock
    behavior (exit 2, last stderr line matches `^wordstat: error: ` — D5);
    catch-all `Exception` → `wordstat: error: internal error`, exit 1 (D6).
  - Success: print `format_text` or `format_json` result to stdout, exit 0.
- `tests/test_cli.py`: subprocess tests via
  `subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "wordstat", *args], capture_output=True,
  input=..., cwd=REPO_ROOT, timeout=30)` comparing raw bytes, plus one in-process
  test of the exit-1 catch-all (monkeypatch `analyze` to raise, call `main()`) so
  every row of the §5.8 table has evidence (PM F1).

## Out of scope:
- Core counting/format logic (T1 owns it; CLI calls `analyze`/`format_*`).
- PYTHONHASHSEED determinism matrix, CRLF/BOM edge fixture suite, stdin-guard
  matrix beyond one smoke case (T3).
- Packaging, console scripts, configuration files.

Module/System:
`wordstat` package CLI layer (`__main__.py`); CLI tests in `tests/test_cli.py`.

## Dependencies:

* T1-core-analysis

## Technical Notes:
- `prog="wordstat"` is load-bearing (§5.6): without it, argparse uses
  `__main__.py` (≤3.13) or `python -m wordstat` (3.14+) and the contract's
  `^wordstat: error: ` prefix breaks. Assert `usage: wordstat` in `--help`.
- `--top` validator (Decision D3): `type=int` alone accepts `--top 0` (verified);
  use a custom callable raising `argparse.ArgumentTypeError`. Rejected values:
  `0`, `-1`, `abc`, `1.5`, missing value → each exit 2. `--top 1` and `--top=5`
  work. Error line shape: `wordstat: error: argument --top: <message>`.
- Usage errors print argparse's usage line(s) THEN the error line; tests assert
  the **last** stderr line against `^wordstat: error: ` (D5), not single-line.
  Exit-3 errors are exactly one stderr line ending in `\n`.
- Error precedence (D7): argparse runs first — `--top 0 missing.txt` exits 2,
  not 3. A missing file with valid args exits 3.
- stdout must be byte-empty (`b""`) on every error path; assert
  `b"Traceback" not in result.stderr` for every error case.
- `-` as FILE is a literal filename (R2: stdin never read) — missing `-` is
  exit 3 `cannot read file`. Extra positionals → exit 2 (unrecognized arguments).
- Reconfigure must happen before I/O (`io.UnsupportedOperation` if the stream was
  already read). Under subprocess tests the streams are real pipes, so reconfigure
  is what makes `\n` bytes deterministic on Windows.
- Derive `REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]` in tests; pass
  `cwd=REPO_ROOT`; never set `PYTHONSAFEPATH` (it would break `-m` resolution).
- Wire `--json` to `format_json`, default to `format_text` (R5); both come from T1.

## Acceptance Criteria:

* `python -m wordstat --help` exits 0 with help on stdout containing
  `usage: wordstat` and empty stderr (AC4).
* Contract example passes through the CLI byte-exactly:
  text golden `lines: 3\nwords: 8\nchars: 33\ntop: cat=2 the=2 a=1\n`;
  `--json --top 2` golden
  `{"lines": 3, "words": 8, "chars": 33, "top": [{"word": "cat", "count": 2}, {"word": "the", "count": 2}]}\n` (AC1).
* Error matrix (AC3): missing file / directory / unreadable → exit 3, stderr
  `wordstat: error: <path>: cannot read file\n`; invalid UTF-8 → exit 3,
  `wordstat: error: <path>: not valid UTF-8\n`; usage errors (no FILE, unknown
  flag, extra arg, bad `--top`) → exit 2 with last stderr line matching
  `^wordstat: error: `; stdout `b""` and no `Traceback` in all error cases.
* `--top` values `0`, `-1`, `abc`, `1.5`, and a missing value each exit 2;
  default `--top` is 3 (AC5).
* Empty file succeeds with zeroed output through the CLI (AC2 smoke).
* stdin is never read: with FILE + piped stdin the output is unchanged; without
  FILE the process exits 2 (no hang) (AC9).
* All tests in `tests/test_cli.py` pass.

* Validation evidence recorded in `tasks/T2-cli-entry-point.notes.md` with

  - CRLF fixture: `"The cat sat.\r\nThe cat ran!\r\nA dog.\r\n"` → `chars: 36`,
    `words: 8`, `lines: 3` (AC10, Decision D1).

Task Name:
T1 — Core analysis module (counting, top words, formatters) with unit tests

Context:
`wordstat` must produce exact counts (R3), exact top-word ordering (R4) and exact
output strings (R5) from decoded text. The pure core is built and pinned by unit
tests before any CLI wiring exists, so the contract's counting/token semantics are
locked down independently of argparse, streams and exit codes. Supports the
contract example and every acceptance criterion about counts and formats
(AC1, AC2, AC7, AC8, AC10) as far as in-process evidence can.

Scope:

In scope:
---
- `wordstat/__init__.py`: pure functions only —
  - `analyze(text: str, top_n: int) -> dict` returning keys in order `lines`,
    `words`, `chars`, `top`, where `top` is a list of `{"word": str, "count": int}`
    (inner keys in that order).
  - `format_text(result: dict) -> str` — exactly four `\n`-terminated lines
    (`lines: `, `words: `, `chars: `, `top: `); empty top line is exactly `top:`
    with no trailing space.
  - `format_json(result: dict) -> str` — `json.dumps(result)` with default
    separators + trailing `\n`.
- `tests/test_core.py`: in-process pytest unit tests for the formulas, the token
  table, splitlines examples, top ordering and both formatters' exact output.

## Out of scope:
- `wordstat/__main__.py`, argparse, exit codes, stream reconfiguration (T2).
- Subprocess/CLI contract tests, determinism matrix, BOM/CRLF fixture files (T3).
- Any deviation from `contract.md` counting semantics (e.g. no `str.isalpha`,
  no `\w` word rule, no Unicode segmentation).

Module/System:
`wordstat/` package pure core (importable without side effects); tests in `tests/`.

## Dependencies:

* None

## Technical Notes:
- Formulas are normative (`feature-specification.md` §5.3): `lines =
  len(text.splitlines())`; `words = len(re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", text.lower()))`;
  `chars = len(text)` on the **original** decoded text — computed BEFORE lowering
  (`len('İ'.lower()) == 2`, so lowering first would corrupt `chars`).

- Build the Kelvin and BOM fixtures from the six-character ASCII escapes
  "\u212A" and "hello\uFEFFworld" (backslash + u + hex
  digits), never by copy-pasting glyphs from the spec table (PM F4 - lookalike
  glyphs hide the wrong code point).
- `chars` counts code points of the decoded text with no newline normalization
  (Decision D1) — a CRLF string's `\r` counts; `analyze` receives the decoded
  string as-is and must not translate anything.

  `--top` (default 3) and is assumed >= 1 (validated at CLI, T2). Fewer distinct
  words than `top_n` lists all (no error).
- `format_json` must use `json.dumps` **default** separators (`", "`, `": "`),
  no `sort_keys`/`indent`/`separators` overrides; dict insertion order provides
  the contract key order. Output of both formatters is pure ASCII for `[a-z0-9]+`
  tokens, but return `str` and let the CLI encode (streams are reconfigured in T2).
- Golden (contract example, trailing newline included): `analyze("The cat sat.\nThe cat ran!\nA dog.\n", 3)` →
  `lines=3, words=8, chars=33`, `top=[cat=2, the=2, a=1]`;
  `format_text` → `lines: 3\nwords: 8\nchars: 33\ntop: cat=2 the=2 a=1\n`;
  `format_json` (top 2) → `{"lines": 3, "words": 8, "chars": 33, "top": [{"word": "cat", "count": 2}, {"word": "the", "count": 2}]}\n`.
- Empty text: `analyze("", n)` → `0, 0, 0`, `top=[]`; `format_text` ends with
  `top:\n`; `format_json` has `"top": []` (Decision D9).

Task Name:
T2 — CLI entry point (argparse, streams, errors, exit codes) with subprocess tests

Context:
With the pure core locked (T1), `wordstat/__main__.py` must expose the exact
command-line contract: `python -m wordstat [--json] [--top N] FILE` from the repo
root, R1/R2/R5/R6 wiring, and the exit-code/error table of `contract.md` — clean
messages on stderr, empty stdout on error, never a traceback. This is the task
that makes the tool invocable and shapes every byte the user sees (AC1, AC3–AC6,
AC9).

Scope:

In scope:
---
- `wordstat/__main__.py`: `main(argv=None) -> int` plus
  `if __name__ == "__main__": raise SystemExit(main())`:
  - Startup: `sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")` and the same
    for `sys.stderr` (R6 + Decision D2), before any read/write.
  - `argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="wordstat")` with `--json` (store_true),
    `--top` (custom `type=` accepting int-strings >= 1, raising
    `argparse.ArgumentTypeError` otherwise; default 3), one required FILE.
  - Read the file as bytes and `decode("utf-8-sig")` (strict, no newline
    translation — Decision D1); never read stdin; `<path>` echoed exactly as given.
  - Error mapping per `contract.md` §Exit codes: OSError → exit 3
    `wordstat: error: <path>: cannot read file`; UnicodeDecodeError → exit 3
    `wordstat: error: <path>: not valid UTF-8`; argparse usage errors keep stock
    behavior (exit 2, last stderr line matches `^wordstat: error: ` — D5);
    catch-all `Exception` → `wordstat: error: internal error`, exit 1 (D6).
  - Success: print `format_text` or `format_json` result to stdout, exit 0.
- `tests/test_cli.py`: subprocess tests via
  `subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "wordstat", *args], capture_output=True,
  input=..., cwd=REPO_ROOT, timeout=30)` comparing raw bytes, plus one in-process
  test of the exit-1 catch-all (monkeypatch `analyze` to raise, call `main()`) so
  every row of the §5.8 table has evidence (PM F1).

## Out of scope:
- Core counting/format logic (T1 owns it; CLI calls `analyze`/`format_*`).
- PYTHONHASHSEED determinism matrix, CRLF/BOM edge fixture suite, stdin-guard
  matrix beyond one smoke case (T3).
- Packaging, console scripts, configuration files.

Module/System:
`wordstat` package CLI layer (`__main__.py`); CLI tests in `tests/test_cli.py`.

## Dependencies:

* T1-core-analysis

## Technical Notes:
- `prog="wordstat"` is load-bearing (§5.6): without it, argparse uses
  `__main__.py` (≤3.13) or `python -m wordstat` (3.14+) and the contract's
  `^wordstat: error: ` prefix breaks. Assert `usage: wordstat` in `--help`.
- `--top` validator (Decision D3): `type=int` alone accepts `--top 0` (verified);
  use a custom callable raising `argparse.ArgumentTypeError`. Rejected values:
  `0`, `-1`, `abc`, `1.5`, missing value → each exit 2. `--top 1` and `--top=5`
  work. Error line shape: `wordstat: error: argument --top: <message>`.
- Usage errors print argparse's usage line(s) THEN the error line; tests assert
  the **last** stderr line against `^wordstat: error: ` (D5), not single-line.
  Exit-3 errors are exactly one stderr line ending in `\n`.
- Error precedence (D7): argparse runs first — `--top 0 missing.txt` exits 2,
  not 3. A missing file with valid args exits 3.
- stdout must be byte-empty (`b""`) on every error path; assert
  `b"Traceback" not in result.stderr` for every error case.
- `-` as FILE is a literal filename (R2: stdin never read) — missing `-` is
  exit 3 `cannot read file`. Extra positionals → exit 2 (unrecognized arguments).
- Reconfigure must happen before I/O (`io.UnsupportedOperation` if the stream was
  already read). Under subprocess tests the streams are real pipes, so reconfigure
  is what makes `\n` bytes deterministic on Windows.
- Derive `REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]` in tests; pass
  `cwd=REPO_ROOT`; never set `PYTHONSAFEPATH` (it would break `-m` resolution).
- Wire `--json` to `format_json`, default to `format_text` (R5); both come from T1.

# Implementation Plan: wordstat

**Feature folder:** `docs/spec-001-feature/`
**Spec:** `feature-specification.md` (requirement source of truth: `contract.md` at repo root)
**Status:** Plan complete — ready for plan-review
**Tasks:** 3 tasks across 1 implementation phase
**Date:** 2026-10-27

---

## 1. Objective

Deliver `wordstat`, a Python 3.11+ stdlib-only CLI, such that `python -m wordstat [--json] [--top N] FILE` run from the repo root behaves exactly as `contract.md` specifies: correct counts (R3), correct top words (R4), exact text/JSON output bytes (R5, §5.5 of the spec), deterministic output on Windows/macOS/Linux (R6), clean specific-exit-code failures with no tracebacks, and `--help` exiting 0 (R1). pytest tests supply the evidence.

## 2. Requirements under delivery

Functional requirements (contract, restated in the spec):

| ID | Requirement | Delivery mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | `--help` exits 0 | argparse `--help` (T2) |
| R2 | Exactly one FILE, decoded `utf-8-sig`, stdin never read | bytes read + `decode('utf-8-sig')` (T2); stdin-guard tests (T3) |
| R3 | `lines`/`words`/`chars` formulas on decoded text | pure `analyze()` (T1) |
| R4 | `top` = N most frequent, count desc then word asc, default 3 | `analyze()` sort key `(-count, word)` (T1) |
| R5 | Text format default; `--json` selects JSON | `format_text`/`format_json` (T1) + CLI flag (T2) |
| R6 | Deterministic UTF-8, `\n`, no locale | `reconfigure` stdout+stderr (T2); determinism tests (T3) |

Acceptance criteria AC1–AC11 of the spec are covered per the coverage matrix in `draft.md`. Decisions D1–D9 (CRLF `chars`, stderr reconfigure, `--top` validator, BOM meaning, usage-error shape, exit-1 message, error precedence, surplus args/`-`, empty-file output) are binding design inputs from `feature-specification.md` §Research Synthesis.

## 3. Architecture and file layout

```
repo root/
  wordstat/
    __init__.py      # pure core (T1): analyze(), format_text(), format_json()
    __main__.py      # CLI (T2): main(argv) -> int; stream reconfigure, argparse, errors
  tests/
    test_core.py     # T1: in-process unit tests of the pure core
    test_cli.py      # T2: subprocess tests of the CLI contract (help, formats, errors)
    test_contract.py # T3: golden byte outputs, edge fixtures, determinism matrix
  docs/spec-001-feature/   # planning package (this run)
```

Design rules (from `feature-specification.md` §5):
- Whole-file bytes read → `bytes.decode('utf-8-sig')` (strict); **no** newline normalization (D1).
- `chars = len(text)` computed before `text.lower()` (U+0130 lengthens on lower).
- Tokens: `re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", text.lower())`; top sorted by `(-count, word)`.
- `json.dumps(obj)` default separators, key order `lines, words, chars, top`; text format exactly four `\n`-terminated lines; empty top line is exactly `top:`.
- `main()` reconfigures stdout **and** stderr to `encoding="utf-8", newline="\n"` before any I/O (D2).
- argparse `prog="wordstat"`; `--top` custom `type=` rejecting `< 1` and non-ints with `ArgumentTypeError` (D3); usage errors keep stock argparse output, exit 2 (D5); read errors exit 3 with exact single-line messages; catch-all `Exception` → `wordstat: error: internal error`, exit 1 (D6).

## 4. Work breakdown

### T1 — Core analysis module (`wordstat/__init__.py`) + unit tests
Pure, CLI-free: `analyze(text, top_n)` returning the JSON-shape dict (`lines`, `words`, `chars`, `top` with `{"word", "count"}` entries in that key order); `format_text(result)`; `format_json(result)`. Unit tests pin the counting formulas, the token table, the splitlines boundary examples, top ordering with ties, and both formatters' exact strings (including bare `top:` and the contract example).

### T2 — CLI entry point (`wordstat/__main__.py`) + CLI tests
`main(argv=None) -> int` with stream reconfigure, argparse wiring (`prog`, `--json`, `--top`, FILE), bytes read + `utf-8-sig` decode, error mapping to the contract's exit-code table, catch-all exit 1. Subprocess tests (`sys.executable -m wordstat`, `cwd=REPO_ROOT`, byte capture) cover `--help`, the contract example in both formats, `--top` validation, the full error matrix (missing/directory/unreadable, invalid UTF-8 variants, usage errors), stdout-empty-on-error, and no-traceback.

### T3 — Contract test matrix & determinism
Golden byte outputs for every format case (incl. empty, BOM-only, BOM+content); edge fixtures written with `Path.write_bytes` (CRLF with pinned `chars: 36` per D1, mid-file U+FEFF, `\x0b`, invalid sequences `b"\xff\xfe"` / `b"\x80"` / `b"\xc3"`); stdin-never-read guard; two-run PYTHONHASHSEED determinism check; full-suite green run; `.gitignore` gains `.pytest_cache/`.

## 5. Sequencing and dependencies

```
T1 (core) ──► T2 (CLI) ──► T3 (contract matrix & determinism)
   └──────────────┴─────────────┘   (T3 also consumes T1 for in-process fixtures)
```

- T1 has no dependencies; T2 depends on T1; T3 depends on T1 and T2.
- One implementation phase: all three tasks form a single phase whose combined requirements are reviewed before advancement (`impl-review` is the final review for the run).

## 6. Validation strategy

Per task (must pass before the next task starts; commands run from repo root):

| Task | Validation command | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | `python -m pytest tests/test_core.py -q` | counting/token/formatter unit results |
| T2 | `python -m pytest tests/test_cli.py -q` | subprocess exit codes + stderr/stdout bytes |
| T3 | `python -m pytest -q` | full suite incl. determinism matrix |

Rules: compare raw `bytes` from `subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True)` (never decoded text); set `cwd` to the repo root and a timeout; never set `PYTHONSAFEPATH`; fixtures are byte-written; pytest is the only test dependency and never imported by the package.

## 7. Risks and mitigations

Carried from `feature-specification.md` §8: Windows `\r\n` translation (mitigated by `newline='\n'` reconfigure + byte asserts); set-iteration nondeterminism (explicit total sort + PYTHONHASHSEED test); argparse `prog` drift across 3.13/3.14 (explicit `prog="wordstat"`); `type=int` accepting `--top 0` (custom type); `lower()` length change (compute `chars` pre-lowering); text-mode newline normalization changing `chars` (bytes decode per D1); pytest capture vs `reconfigure` (subprocess-only byte claims).

## 8. Out of scope / deferred

Streaming large files, Unicode/locale segmentation, packaging/PyPI, multi-file or stdin input, any change to `contract.md` (spec NG1–NG5).

## 9. Definition of Done (package)

- All three tasks Done with their validation commands green and evidence recorded in `tasks/Tx-*.notes.md`.
- AC1–AC11 demonstrated by tests; `python -m pytest -q` fully green from the repo root.
- Package imports stdlib only; errors never raise a traceback; exit codes match the contract table exactly.
- Phase review READY TO ADVANCE; final `impl-review` PASS.

# References — wordstat planning package

Everything an implementer needs, with descriptions and instructions. Paths are
relative to the repository root unless marked otherwise.

## Requirement sources (authoritative)

| Artifact | Role |
|---|---|
| `contract.md` | **Authoritative interface contract.** R1–R6, command line, both output formats, exit-code table, the worked example. Nothing in this package may change what it requires. |
| `brief.md` | One-paragraph framing: tiny stdlib CLI, deterministic, clean failures, pytest tests. |

## Design documents

| Artifact | Role |
|---|---|
| `docs/spec-001-feature/feature-specification.md` | Frozen requirements + design (§5 detailed design, §8 risks, §9 ACs, §Research Synthesis with decisions D1–D9 and assumptions A1–A9). The normative reading of the contract for implementation. |
| `docs/spec-001-feature/implementation-plan.md` | Frozen plan: architecture, work breakdown T1–T3, sequencing, validation strategy, package DoD. |
| `docs/spec-001-feature/draft.md` | Frozen coverage matrix: every requirement/goal/AC → task mapping, plus the decisions table. Use it to check you are not missing a requirement. |
| `docs/spec-001-feature/review-development-project-manager.md` | PM review (APPROVED WITH NOTES) + orchestrator gap resolution table. Read F1–F10 to see what was tightened and why. |

## Tracking (mutable during implement)

| Artifact | Role |
|---|---|
| `docs/spec-001-feature/kanban.md` | Lane status (single source of truth). Backlog/Ready/In Progress/In Review/Blocked/Done + Validation Checklist release gate. Update on every move; run `validate-kanban`. |
| `docs/spec-001-feature/handoff.md` | Running log: decisions D1–D9 with reasons, session summaries, blockers. Append a line naming each task ID on every Done or Blocked move. |
| `docs/spec-001-feature/tasks/Tx-*.notes.md` | Per-task notes (writable): validation evidence — commands, outputs, revision. Write before the Done move. |

## Tasks (frozen bodies — execute in this order)

| Task | File | Delivers | Gate before next task |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | `tasks/T1-core-analysis.md` | `wordstat/__init__.py` pure core (`analyze`, `format_text`, `format_json`) + `tests/test_core.py` | `python -m pytest tests/test_core.py -q` |
| T2 | `tasks/T2-cli-entry-point.md` | `wordstat/__main__.py` (argparse, streams, errors, exit codes) + `tests/test_cli.py` | `python -m pytest tests/test_core.py tests/test_cli.py -q` |
| T3 | `tasks/T3-contract-test-matrix.md` | `tests/test_contract.py` goldens/edge fixtures/determinism + `.gitignore` housekeeping | `python -m pytest -q` |

Dependencies: T1 none → T2 (T1) → T3 (T1, T2). One implementation phase; phase review covers all three; final acceptance is `impl-review`.

## Product files to create

| File | Owner | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `wordstat/__init__.py` | T1 | Pure, import-side-effect-free core. Stdlib only (`re`, `collections`, `json`). |
| `wordstat/__main__.py` | T2 | `main(argv=None) -> int`; `raise SystemExit(main())` guard. Stream reconfigure, argparse, I/O, error mapping. |

## Test files to create

| File | Owner | Focus |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/test_core.py` | T1 | Counting formulas, token table, splitlines edges, top ordering, formatter goldens (in-process). |
| `tests/test_cli.py` | T2 | Subprocess byte contract: `--help`, goldens, `--top` validation, full error matrix, exit-1 catch-all (in-process), stdin ignored. |
| `tests/test_contract.py` | T3 | Golden bytes for every format case, BOM/CRLF/invalid-UTF-8 fixtures, non-ASCII path stderr (D2), PYTHONHASHSEED determinism, AST stdlib-only check. |

## Implementation instructions

1. **Environment:** Python 3.11+ (dev host: 3.13.15). Before T1's gate:
   `python -c "import pytest"` — else `pip install pytest` (test-only dependency).
2. **Run order:** T1 → T2 → T3. Respect `Dependencies:`. Promote each task
   Backlog → Ready in `kanban.md` when its prerequisites are Done (one lane per
   edit), then Ready → In Progress when work starts.
3. **Per task:** implement the minimum code, run the task's gate command from the
   repo root, record evidence (commands, outputs, revision) in
   `tasks/Tx-<name>.notes.md`, then move through In Review to Done. In the Done
   step: move to Done, run `check-dod --path docs/spec-001-feature --task <ID>`,
   and on failure move back and fix.
4. **Key binding decisions** (full text in `feature-specification.md` §Research
   Synthesis): D1 bytes decode (no newline normalization; CRLF `\r` counts) ·
   D2 stderr reconfigured like stdout · D3 custom `--top` type (>= 1) ·
   D4 BOM excluded at start only · D5 usage errors keep argparse shape (assert
   last stderr line) · D6 catch-all exit 1 `wordstat: error: internal error` ·
   D7 usage errors precede file access · D8 one FILE, `-` literal · D9 empty file
   → zeroed counts, bare `top:` / `"top": []`.
5. **Determinism rules:** reconfigure before any I/O; explicit `(-count, word)`
   sort; `json.dumps` defaults; compare raw bytes in tests; never set
   `PYTHONSAFEPATH`; fixtures via `Path.write_bytes`.
6. **Gates (plugin scripts):** from the plugin root
   (`.../plugin/geeky-orchestration/scripts/`): `check-commit.py --message`
   before every commit; `validate-kanban.py --path docs/spec-001-feature` after
   every lane move; `check-dod.py --path docs/spec-001-feature --task <ID>` in
   the Done step; `validate-task-schema.py` / `validate-planning-folder.py` at
   stage boundaries. Never push; never `--no-verify`/`--force`/`--amend`.
7. **Out of scope:** streaming, Unicode segmentation, packaging, stdin/multi-file
   input, any change to `contract.md`. The orchestrator never edits product code
   or tests — fixes go through `geeky-coder`.

1	# Geeky Implement Execution Protocol
2	
3	# geeky-implement
4	
5	geeky orchestrator that executes the geeky-plan package — drives tasks through the kanban, delegates geeky-coder + reviewer subagents, validates, commits per phase, and keeps handoff.md current. This is the *runtime* counterpart to the `geeky-plan` skill's *planning*.
6	
7	## Input
8	
9	`$ARGUMENTS`: a folder produced by `geeky-plan` containing at minimum `implementation-plan.md`, `kanban.md`, `tasks/Tx-*.md`, `handoff.md`, `references.md`.
10	
11	**Pre-run preflight (STEP ZERO, always):** self-test the tooling before trusting it — `preflight.ps1` on Windows / `preflight.py` elsewhere, passing `-Path/--path <folder>`. It verifies the validators' own dependencies and compilability (a gate script crashing at import time once stalled a 91-hour run), checks handoff/kanban freshness, detects an active `.heartbeat` from a prior run, and reminds about pre-run re-auth for long runs. If it exits non-zero: STOP and report. If any *later* validator crashes mid-run (traceback rather than a clean fail), surface it in one line, manually check the same criteria, and continue or stop VISIBLY — never absorb a crash into a silent stall.
12	
13	**Pre-run validation (FIRST STEP, always):** invoke the bundled validator. Pick the runtime by host OS (`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` is the root of the `geeky-orchestration` plugin):
14	
15	- **Windows (preferred):**
16	  ```
17	  pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/validate-planning-folder.ps1" -Path "<folder>"
18	  ```
19	- **macOS / Linux / any host with Python 3:**
20	  ```
21	  python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/validate-planning-folder.py" --path "<folder>"
22	  ```
23	  (Use `python3` if `python` is not on PATH.)
24	
25	Both produce identical output and exit codes. If it exits non-zero, print its output and STOP. Do not attempt to regenerate planning artifacts — that is the `geeky-plan` skill's job. If the folder is missing entirely, ask the user.
26	
27	**Scripts over MCP tools:** always prefer these bundled scripts to the `geeky_*` MCP tools — the MCP tools trigger per-call permission prompts mid-run and are subject to the `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` interpolation bug. Use the MCP tools only when the scripts are genuinely unavailable. If `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` is not interpolated in your environment, resolve the plugin root yourself (installed cache: `~/.claude/plugins/cache/<marketplace>/geeky-orchestration/<version>/`; or the source checkout) — do not stall on the placeholder.
28	
29	Optional inline flags inside `$ARGUMENTS` (parse loosely from the string):
30	- `--phase=<name|number>` — scope this run to a single phase from `implementation-plan.md`. Default: run all Ready tasks through to Done or Blocked.
31	- `--dry-run` — produce the execution plan + parallelization decisions only; do not call coders or modify files.
32	- `--serial` — disable parallel execution for this run (override the default cap of 3).
33	
34	## Context
35	
36	To execute the planning package produced by `geeky-plan`: walk the kanban, delegate implementation to `geeky-coder` subagents, validate, run code review and phase review, consolidate findings, and keep the kanban, handoff, and per-task notes current.
37	
38	Operating profile (DO NOT prompt to change mid-run; only respect inline flags above):
39	
40	- **Autonomy:** fully autonomous from start until the backlog is empty, a task is moved to Blocked, or a validation/review step cannot be auto-resolved. Do not pause for confirmation between tasks.
41	- **Session grain:** default ONE phase per session. At each phase boundary: checkpoint `handoff.md`, set `.heartbeat` to `paused`, and prefer resuming in a fresh session over pushing through context compaction or token expiry. If the user explicitly asks for a full multi-phase run in one session, honor it — but remind them of the >1h re-auth preflight first.
42	- **Heartbeat:** maintain `<folder>/.heartbeat` (JSON `{"ts":"<ISO-8601 UTC>","task":"T<x>","status":"running|paused|done"}`). Write `running` at run start, refresh `ts`+`task` on EVERY lane move (same moments you update kanban), set `paused` on deliberate mid-run stop, `done` at run end. External watchdog hooks key on this file — a stale `running` heartbeat is how a dead run gets detected.
43	- **Review boundaries:** task review answers whether the task meets its ACs and passes its defined tests. Phase review checks the complete phase requirements and decides whether the next phase may start; the last phase is reviewed like any other. One reviewer dispatch at phase end does both (step 14). Final implementation review belongs to `impl-review` and does not replace any phase review; do not add another final-review layer.
44	- **Commits:** commit per phase, split into multiple small logically-grouped commits, one concern per commit; each functional delivery groups its required code and tests (step 16). **NEVER push to remote.** Never `--no-verify`, never amend, never force.
45	- **Parallelism:** up to 3 concurrent `geeky-coder` subagents when safe (see Parallelization Rules). Otherwise serial.
46	- **Main-thread budget:** workers return at most ~15 lines (verdict, files, evidence summary) and write detail to the task notes. The validation evidence (tested revision, exact commands and their result lines) is always returned in full and does not count toward the limit; review verdicts are never shortened. Read successful command output through a tail (e.g. `Select-Object -Last 20`); read a failure in full. Do not re-read files a worker already summarised. Do each task's close-out (notes, lane move, gates, handoff line) in one tool call, still one lane per edit. Dispatch independent work in the same turn.
47	
48	## Constitution
49	
50	**DO THIS SEQUENTIALLY IN THIS ORDER.** All artifact reads and writes happen inside the folder passed in `$ARGUMENTS` (the planning package folder), except for the actual code changes which happen in the project tree the planning folder belongs to.
51	
52	Hard rules — violations are bugs:
53	
54	1. **Never modify** `implementation-plan.md`, `feature-specification.md`, `draft.md`, `references.md`, or any `tasks/Tx-*.md` file body. These are the planning contract. The bundled PreToolUse guard will warn if you try. If a task is wrong, add a note in `kanban.md` under Blocked and surface to the user.
55	2. **Always update** `kanban.md` on every lane move and `handoff.md` on every task completion or block.
56	3. **Never push** to a remote. Never use `--no-verify`, `--force`, or `--amend`.
57	4. **Respect declared dependencies.** A task is only eligible when every entry in its `Dependencies:` block is in the Done lane of `kanban.md`, or is In Review in the current phase with passing validation evidence (its review comes in the phase review).
58	5. **Stop on Blocked.** When any task moves to Blocked, finalize state (handoff, kanban) and return to the user with a summary. Do not silently skip blocked tasks to keep going.
59	6. **One source of truth for status:** `kanban.md`. If `handoff.md` and `kanban.md` disagree, trust kanban and reconcile handoff.
60	7. **Delegate implementation using the canonical `geeky-coder` instructions.** Check the live harness role catalog before dispatch. A TOML file or generated projection does not prove the role is callable. If the role is unavailable, do not retry guessed or namespaced variants. Use an available generic role with the canonical agent body and task brief, preserving requested model settings. If the user requires the registered role itself, report the registration blocker instead of substituting it.
61	8. **The orchestrator never edits product code or tests.** Every fix, including a reviewer's one-line suggestion, goes to `geeky-coder`. Non-blocking findings go to follow-ups.
62	
63	## Cross-task consequences
64	
65	Record a consequence for another task in the affected task's notes and in `handoff.md`, and notify an active worker when its work must change.
66	
67	## Tasks
68	
69	### Phase 0 — Load and analyze the planning package
70	
71	1. Run the bundled validators (see Input). On failure, stop. In addition to the planning-folder validator, run the **task-file schema** gate now — it is the plan→implement boundary check (`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` is the plugin root; `.ps1` on Windows, `.py` elsewhere; full matrix in `AGENTS.md` / `geeky.manifest.json`):
72	
73	    ```
74	    python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/validate-task-schema.py" --path "<folder>"
75	    ```
76	
77	    If it exits non-zero, the task files are malformed — stop and surface to the user (do not silently fix frozen task bodies).
78	
79	2. Read every file in the planning folder: `implementation-plan.md`, `kanban.md`, `references.md`, `handoff.md`, `feature-specification.md`, `draft.md`, the most recent `review-*.md`, and every file in `tasks/`. Use `TaskCreate` to track this run's own phases so progress is visible to the user.
80	
81	2b. **Resume detection (idempotent re-entry).** This skill must be safe to re-invoke after a session cutoff, compaction, or interrupted run — re-invocation continues, never restarts:
82	   - Tasks in **Done** stay done. Never re-execute them, never re-run their validation, never redo their commits.
83	   - Tasks stuck in **In Progress** with no live coder are orphans from a cut-off run. Reconcile each against ground truth (git status/log, the declared file surface, any `tasks/Tx-*.notes.md`): if the work appears complete, verify saved validation evidence first and run only missing, invalidated, unreliable or explicitly required independent checks, then route it through review → Done normally; if partial or absent, move it back to Ready with a kanban note (`<!-- reset from orphaned in_progress: YYYY-MM-DD -->`).
84	   - If `handoff.md` ends with a `RESUME:` line (see step 17), trust it as the starting hint but verify against kanban (kanban is the source of truth).
85	   - Then proceed with the normal eligibility walk — it naturally continues from wherever the previous run stopped.
86	
87	3. Build an in-memory execution model:
88	   - **Task graph** — node per `Tx-*.md`, edges from each task's `Dependencies:` block.
89	   - **Phase grouping** — derive from `implementation-plan.md` headings if it has explicit phases, else from kanban grouping comments, else by dependency layer (tasks with no unmet deps = layer 0, etc.).
90	   - **File-overlap inference** — for each task, scan its `In scope` / `Module/System` / `Technical Notes` for filenames, modules, or package paths. Two tasks are file-conflicting if their declared surfaces overlap.
91	   - **Eligibility** — task is eligible iff it sits in kanban Ready AND every dependency is Done, or is In Review in the current phase with passing validation evidence.
92	
93	4. If `--dry-run` is set, print the execution model (phase order, per-phase batches, parallel groups with justifications) and STOP. Otherwise continue.
94	
95	### Phase 1 — Execute each phase
96	
97	For each phase, in plan order:
98	
99	5. **Select the next batch** of eligible tasks. Before dispatch and at every phase boundary, consume optional `GEEKY_DEADLINE_UTC` (UTC timestamp) and `GEEKY_CLOSEOUT_RESERVE_S` (nonnegative seconds within the hard budget). When both are absent, continue normally. With context present, calculate remaining time; within the advisory reserve prioritize required acceptance and closeout over optional work. If insufficient time remains for required work, save exact incomplete task/review state, evidence and next command in notes/handoff, pause the heartbeat and stop dispatching. Invalid context must be reported and checkpointed, never treated as extra allowance. Deadline or reserve expiry never establishes acceptance, moves an unmet task to Done, or substitutes for a required reviewer/gate. Batch size = min(3, eligible count, parallelism flag). A batch is parallel-safe iff:
100	   - no task in the batch depends on another task in the batch, AND
101	   - no two tasks in the batch have overlapping declared file surfaces, AND
102	   - none of them is marked P0-blocker-for-others in the implementation plan.
103	   Otherwise reduce batch size or fall back to serial. Record the justification in the per-task notes file (step 10).
104	
105	6. **Move every task in the batch from Ready to In Progress** in `kanban.md`. Add a timestamp comment beside each: `<!-- in_progress: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM -->`. Refresh `.heartbeat` (`ts` = now, `task` = batch's first task ID, `status` = `running`).
106	
107	7. **Delegate implementation to `geeky-coder`.** When the batch has >1 task, send a SINGLE message with multiple `Agent` tool calls in parallel (this is required — do not serialize parallel work into separate messages). Each brief must be self-contained:
108	   - Full text of the task file (paste it — coders don't share your context).
109	   - **Verified absolute paths** for every file/folder the brief references — verify each exists (Glob/ls) before writing the brief; never pass an assumed path. Subagents don't share your context or memory, and assumed paths are a top wasted-turn cause.
110	   - Pointers to relevant sections of `implementation-plan.md` and `feature-specification.md` by heading + line range, not just filename.
111	   - Acceptance criteria copied verbatim.
112	   - The validation block from the task file (`Tests/Validation Before Next Task`). Resolve uncertain prerequisites with the smallest useful check before committing to broader work. Reuse established methods and valid evidence. Preserve required ordering and acceptance gates; an early diagnostic result does not replace them.
113	   - Explicit instruction: *do not modify files outside the declared In Scope surface; if you discover the scope is wrong, stop and report — do not silently expand.*
114	   - Give the worker authority to finish the bounded assignment, including compatible fixes and required checks. Ask for a consolidated return; interrupt only for blockers, scope decisions or ownership conflicts, not each small edit. Contact the worker only for new information, a blocker, a decision or a completed result; use completion waits instead of repeated status requests. User progress updates do not require another worker round trip.
115	   - Use the harness's actual dispatch schema and callable role name. Apply the canonical-instructions fallback above only when needed; record the substitution once.
116	   - The absolute path of `tasks/Tx-*.notes.md`, where the worker writes its detail, and a return limit of ~15 lines (see Main-thread budget).
117	
118	8. **Verify the task's validation evidence** after each coder returns. Require the tested revision or file hashes, exact commands, exit status and results. Inspect the saved output through a tail; a bare claim of PASS is insufficient. Reuse passing evidence for unchanged code, dependencies and relevant environment. Execute missing checks or rerun only when evidence is invalidated, unreliable, or independent execution is explicitly required. Before repeating a test or review, record what changed or remains unproved, which evidence is invalidated, and the smallest check that resolves it. Reuse valid evidence unless a required check is missing or independent execution is explicitly mandated. If a required command fails:
119	   - Capture the failure output.
120	   - Re-delegate to `geeky-coder` once with the failure context for a fix attempt.
121	   - If it still fails, move the task to **Blocked** with a kanban note that includes the validation command and the failure summary, finalize state per the Constitution, and return to the user.
122	
123	9. **Move the task from In Progress to In Review** once its validation evidence passes. It waits there for the phase review (step 14); do not dispatch a per-task review. Its dependents in this phase may start now (step 3 eligibility).
124	
125	10. **Write a per-task notes file** `tasks/Tx-*.notes.md` (creating it if the worker has not, NOT editing the original task file) containing:
126	    - Parallelization decision and justification.
127	    - Coder summary (one paragraph).
128	    - Validation results (command + pass/fail).
129	    - Review findings, grouped by severity.
130	    - Resolution: which findings were fixed in this run vs deferred (with rationale).
131	    - Final diff scope (list of touched files).
132	    Keep review scope, any reopened evidence and the next action in these existing notes. Do not create another ledger or approval gate.
133	
134	11. **Resolve findings:** send blocking findings from the phase review to `geeky-coder`, batching compatible in-scope fixes into one assignment per owner. Respect dependencies and shared files; do not dispatch one correction at a time when they can be fixed together. Rerun affected checks; dependents of a changed task re-run their validation. Re-review only the affected tasks, in one dispatch, against the changed scope plus the original findings. Preserve unaffected evidence. Blockers and majors within the review contract must be resolved before Done; record unrelated findings separately. Log deferred minors and nits in `handoff.md`.
135	
136	Acceptance must wait until all required tests have passing evidence, even when the task is not in the Blocked lane. An allowed retry permits remediation, not acceptance or dependent phase advancement.
137	
138	12. **Move to Done** in `kanban.md` only after the phase review clears (steps 14–15): validation is green AND the task has a PASS verdict AND no blocker/major findings remain. The **Definition-of-Done** gate verifies the task in the Done lane, so run it in the same step as the Done move, followed by the **kanban-integrity** gate. If `check-dod` does not exit 0, move the task back and fix before trying again; never leave a task in Done with a failing gate. Fix until both exit 0:
139	
140	    ```
141	    python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/check-dod.py" --path "<folder>" --task T<x>
142	    python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/validate-kanban.py" --path "<folder>"
143	    ```
144	
145	    `check-dod` also prints the task's validation block. Match it to the verified evidence from step 8; printing the commands does not require another execution. Run `validate-kanban` after every lane move, not only at Done, so the board never drifts from truth. Refresh `.heartbeat` on the Done move. If either gate CRASHES (traceback / missing module rather than a clean non-zero): say so in one line, run the equivalent manual check (read the DoD block and verify each item; eyeball lane membership), record the crash in the per-task notes, and continue VISIBLY — a crashed gate must never become a silent stall.
146	
147	13. **Repeat steps 5–10** until the current phase has no eligible Ready tasks left, then go to step 14. Steps 11–12 run on the phase review's findings and verdicts.
148	
149	### Phase 2 — End of phase: phase review + commits
150	
151	14. **Phase review** at the end of every phase, including the last; `impl-review` does not replace it. Dispatch ONE `geeky-orchestration:code-reviewer` subagent that reviews every task in the phase and issues the phase verdict. If the phase has more than 4 tasks, or its diff is too large to review AC by AC in one pass, split it into dispatches of at most 4 related tasks; the last dispatch issues the phase verdict using the others' task verdicts as inputs. The **READY TO ADVANCE** or **BLOCKED** verdict must come from that subagent, never from the orchestrator; record its agent ID in the step-17 `handoff.md` phase block. Brief it with:
152	    - Phase name and the phase's task IDs (In Review, plus any already Done).
153	    - For each task: the task template, ACs and validation evidence.
154	    - The aggregated diff for the phase (`git diff` from the phase's starting commit to HEAD).
155	    - The per-task notes files for the phase.
156	    - The relevant section of `implementation-plan.md`.
157	
158	    **Task verdicts** — one per task, kept separate:
159	    - The decision is: **Does this task meet every AC and pass its defined tests?** Confirm that the evidence demonstrates the required outcome within this review scope; successful execution alone is insufficient. Return an AC-by-AC result, test result and PASS or NEEDS FIXES. Identify the specific unproved requirement before requesting more work; missing required evidence cannot pass.
160	    - Inspect immediate dependencies only as needed to answer that question. Do not review the entire implementation chain or add acceptance requirements. Route unrelated findings separately; block a task only when a finding prevents its contract from being met or makes acceptance unsafe under an existing requirement.
161	    - Every blocking finding must cite the violated AC, defined test or existing mandatory constraint, concrete evidence, and the smallest necessary correction. Severity alone does not authorize extra scope. Record optional improvements as follow-ups.
162	    - Return one complete finding set per task, grouped by severity.
163	
164	    **Phase verdict** — review the complete phase requirements, combined behavior, cross-task interactions, shared contracts and phase-level validation, using the task verdicts as inputs. Answer explicitly: **Can we move to the next phase?** Return **READY TO ADVANCE** or **BLOCKED**, with evidence for requirement coverage and any unmet requirement or dependency. All phase tasks must be accounted for; an unfinished required task cannot pass this gate.
165	
166	15. **Integrate phase findings** using step 11. Resolve failures within the approved scope; the re-review dispatch covers only the affected tasks and returns an updated verdict for that same phase before Done. An earlier phase's READY verdict cannot clear a later BLOCKED phase. Do not repeat task reviews without changed code or dependencies, contradictory evidence or a concrete defect affecting the phase. Do not start the next phase until **READY TO ADVANCE** is recorded in the step-17 `handoff.md` phase block. If a blocker cannot be resolved under the existing task contracts, mark Blocked and return with the exact unmet requirement. Minors that do not prevent advancement remain deferred. Then move each cleared task to Done (step 12) before committing.
167	
168	16. **Commit the phase diff, split into multiple small logically-grouped commits.** Decide grouping by reading the diff yourself; each functional delivery includes its required code and tests. Before accepting a committed task snapshot, compare its code, tests and relevant dependencies with the tested revision/file hashes from step 8. Matching inputs and relevant environment permit evidence reuse; missing tests or mismatched inputs require affected validation in an isolated tree at that snapshot. A later final-HEAD pass cannot justify an earlier snapshot. Preserve existing task/Done commit selection (H1); do not rewrite anchors to obtain a pass. Save full commit IDs, exact commands, exit codes and results in the task notes. Each commit message format:
169	
170	    ```
171	    feat(<phase-short-name>): <what this commit changes>
172	
173	    Tasks: T<x>
174	    Refs: docs/<planning-folder>/tasks/Tx-*.md
175	    ```
176	
177	    Name several tasks on the `Tasks:` line only when their changes form one concern.
178	
179	    Use HEREDOC to pass multiline messages. Do NOT push. Do NOT amend. If a pre-commit hook fails, have `geeky-coder` fix any product code or test cause, then create a NEW commit — do not skip hooks.
180	
181	    Before each commit, validate the message with the **commit gate** (`--message` works in PowerShell and bash; in bash you may pipe the message via stdin instead). A non-zero exit blocks that commit: fix the message and re-run the gate until it exits 0, then commit.
182	
183	    ```
184	    python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/check-commit.py" --message "<msg>"
185	    printf '%s' "$msg" | python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/check-commit.py"   # bash alternative
186	    ```
187	
188	17. **Update `handoff.md`** with a phase summary block:
189	    - Phase name, date, duration.
190	    - Tasks completed, tasks blocked (if any).
191	    - Commits created (short SHAs).
192	    - Phase review verdict, reviewer agent ID, supporting evidence and any advancement blockers.
193	    - Deferred follow-ups added in this phase.
194	    - End with a single checkpoint line so any future session can resume with zero re-prompting: `RESUME: <next phase or "run complete"> — next eligible: <task IDs or none>`. Replace the previous `RESUME:` line each time (it is a cursor, not a log).
195	
196	### Phase 3 — End of run
197	
198	18. When all phases complete (or backlog is empty, or a task is blocked):
199	    - When all phases are accepted, route final implementation review to [impl-review](../../impl-review/SKILL.md). Invoke it when final review is authorized by the request or standing workflow; otherwise record it as the next step. Do not substitute another final review or claim final acceptance before its verdict. A phase-only run does not trigger package-wide review.
200	    - Once the authorized gates pass, finish required closeout and report completion. Do not add discretionary hardening, broader tests or another review. Reopen only for evidence of an unmet approved requirement or mandatory constraint; record optional work as a follow-up.
201	    - Append a "Run Summary" section to `handoff.md` with: total tasks completed, total commits, blocked items, deferred follow-ups, suggested next-session start steps.
202	    - Reconcile `kanban.md` lanes and counts with task evidence and the original task count; record current required task, phase and authorized final-review verdicts. An incomplete review or interrupted closeout remains incomplete.
203	    - Only then set `.heartbeat` `status` to `done` if required work and closeout are complete; otherwise set `paused` with a truthful resume block, including interrupted or Blocked state.
204	    - Print to the user: a short status (Done count, Blocked count, Deferred count) and the path to the updated handoff. Suggest the `geeky-status` skill (`/geeky-status <folder>`) as the lightweight follow-up.
205	    - State review and gate claims only as recorded in `handoff.md`, citing reviewer agent IDs. Check each final claim against its source and reviewed scope: distinguish direct function-call coverage from subprocess/CLI coverage, and Git object IDs from file SHA-256 digests. Missing one coverage form does not mean all coverage is absent. List any skipped or self-issued gate under Deviations.
206	
207	## Parallelization rules
208	
209	When deciding whether to parallelize a batch, apply this checklist explicitly and write the result to the per-task notes file:
210	
211	| Check | Pass condition |
212	|---|---|
213	| Declared dependencies | No task in batch depends on another task in batch (transitively) |
214	| File-surface overlap | Pairwise intersection of declared In Scope files/modules is empty |
215	| Shared mutable artifacts | None of the tasks edit the same migration, lockfile, or generated bundle |
216	| Coordination cost | Tasks are conceptually independent — a reviewer can review them without needing to read the other |
217	| Resource ceiling | Total concurrent coders ≤ 3 (or 1 if `--serial`) |
218	
219	If any check fails for a candidate pair, demote to serial for that pair.
220	
221	Task reviews run together inside the phase review, on stable diffs. Tests or reviewer probes that mutate the same database, fixtures, ports or files must be isolated or serialized.
222	
223	Batch independent reads and compatible checks in one dispatch. A shared validation run may satisfy several tasks only when its command, configuration and tested revision meet each task's contract; retain a result for every task. Collect independent failures before remediation when safe. Stop dependent or destructive checks on failure. Separate product defects from harness and environment faults, then fix each compatible set together. Reserve broad final gates for a stable candidate unless the plan explicitly requires them earlier.
224	
225	## Failure modes
226	
227	After two unsuccessful correction cycles on the same issue, diagnose the cause before repeating the approach: product defect, test expectation, harness/fixture, environment, or unresolved requirement. Record the cause and bounded next action in existing notes. This does not grant extra retries or waive a failed gate; any earlier stop condition still applies.
228	
229	These are recoverable — handle inline, do not stop the run:
230	- Coder reports a typo or import error → re-delegate once with the error log.
231	- Pre-commit hook fails on whitespace/lint → route the fix to `geeky-coder` and create a new commit.
232	- Code-review surfaces minor/nit findings → log under Deferred, proceed.
233	- A gate/validator script CRASHES (traceback, missing module) → one-line surface, manual check of the same criteria, note it, continue; flag the plugin for a fix at run end. Never a silent stall.
234	- 401/auth-expiry symptoms mid-run → FIRST append a resume block to `handoff.md` (current task, exact state, next command) and set `.heartbeat` to `paused`; the session may be unrecoverable and the handoff is what survives.
235	- API-error interruption (`<synthetic>` model turn in the log = the API cut the turn off, no auto-resume; external, not your fault) → FIRST checkpoint (`handoff.md` + `.heartbeat` `paused`), then resume — the fix depends on the subtype, so read the turn's text:
236	  - **spend/usage limit** ("hit your monthly spend limit") → raise it at claude.ai/settings/usage or wait; a `/model` switch does NOT help (account-level quota).
237	  - **session limit** ("hit your session limit — resets …") → wait for the reset; `/model` does not help.
238	  - **401 / auth** ("run /login") → re-auth; the session may be unrecoverable, so the handoff is what survives.
239	  - **529 / overloaded** (genuine capacity) → `/model` switch (capacity is per-model) or wait; status.claude.com. Upstream: anthropics/claude-code #60577, #35801.
240	
241	**Diagnosing a quiet/stalled run** — when a run has gone silent, check causes in THIS order (cheapest first; the first is external, not model quality):
242	1. **API-error interruption** — scan the session log tail for `<synthetic>` model turns (NOT for the string "529" — in this environment the real population is spend-limit / session-limit / 401; a genuine 529/overload has not actually occurred here). Fix per subtype above.
243	2. **Validator/gate crash** — a gate scripted itself into a traceback and the loop absorbed it.
244	3. **Logic/plan problem** — only after ruling out the external causes above. Misattributing an external interruption to "the model got stuck" wastes a wrong-fix cycle.
245	
246	These STOP the run (mark Blocked, update handoff, return to user):
247	- A task's validation block fails after one retry.
248	- Code review surfaces a blocker that the coder cannot fix in one follow-up.
249	- Phase review remains BLOCKED after bounded remediation, or requires a change to the approved task contracts.
250	- A task's declared scope is materially wrong (file doesn't exist, dependency missing from plan).
251	- Any merge conflict between parallel coders (this means the parallelization decision was wrong — record the lesson in the notes file).
252	
253	## Acceptance criteria
254	
255	A successful run leaves the folder in this state:
256	
257	1. `kanban.md` reflects current truth — every task is in exactly one lane, Done tasks have `[x]`, In Progress / Blocked tasks carry a timestamp comment.
258	2. `handoff.md` has a new "Run Summary" section at the bottom plus per-phase entries.
259	3. `tasks/Tx-*.notes.md` exists for every task touched in this run.
260	4. The project tree has commits (none pushed) that map cleanly to the phases executed.
261	5. No edits to `implementation-plan.md`, `feature-specification.md`, `draft.md`, `references.md`, or original `tasks/Tx-*.md` files.
262	6. If anything was blocked, the user sees a clear "Blocked: T<x> — <reason>" line and knows where to look.
263	7. `.heartbeat` is finalized (`done`, or `paused` with a matching resume block in `handoff.md`) — never left as a stale `running`.
264	
265	A `--dry-run` invocation must produce the execution model output and modify nothing.
266	
267
